title: XMS, the extended memory driver functions
covers: The functions of the XMS driver, reached through the far entry point that INT 2Fh AX=4310h returns and selected by AH.

rows.text: The XMS driver's AH=00h function gets the version number.
AX is the XMS version in BCD, with the major version in AH and the minor in AL.
BX is the driver's internal revision number.
DX is 0001h when the high memory area exists and 0000h when it does not.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_GET_VERSION of its switch on AH.
The XMS driver's AH=01h function requests the high memory area.
DX is the memory wanted in bytes for a TSR or device driver, or FFFFh for an application program.
AX is 0001h on success and 0000h on failure.
On failure, BL is the error code 80h, 81h, 90h, 91h or 92h.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_ALLOCATE_HIGH_MEMORY of its switch on AH.
When the HMA exists and is free, DX is compared with the configured minimum allocation and any DX at or above it takes the HMA; FFFFh is not treated apart.
When no HMA exists, the request is refused with 90h.
When the application or the DOS kernel already holds the HMA, the request is refused with 91h.
The XMS driver's AH=02h function releases the high memory area.
AX is 0001h on success and 0000h on failure.
On failure, BL is the error code 80h, 81h, 90h or 93h.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_FREE_HIGH_MEMORY of its switch on AH.
When the DOS kernel occupies the HMA, the case logs a warning and still frees the area if an application holds it.
The XMS driver's AH=03h function enables the A20 line globally for the HMA.
AX is 0001h on success and 0000h on failure.
On an error, BL is 80h, 81h or 82h.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_GLOBAL_ENABLE_A20 of its switch on AH.
The local enable runs only when no global enable is in effect; a repeat call stores 0 in the result and takes no further action.
SET_RESULT stores 0001h in AX and 00h in BL on every call, since the local enable always returns 0.
The XMS driver's AH=04h function disables the A20 line globally.
AX is 0001h on success and 0000h on failure.
On an error, BL is 80h, 81h, 82h or 94h.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_GLOBAL_DISABLE_A20 of its switch on AH.
The local disable runs only when a global enable is in effect; a repeat call stores 0 in the result.
SET_RESULT also stores 00h in BL on a success, a case the list does not give.
The XMS driver's AH=05h function enables the A20 line locally.
AX is 0001h on success and 0000h on failure.
On an error, BL is 80h, 81h or 82h.
The function is used for direct access to extended memory.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_LOCAL_ENABLE_A20 of its switch on AH.
SET_RESULT stores 0001h in AX and 00h in BL on every call, since the local enable always returns 0.
The XMS driver's AH=06h function disables the A20 line locally.
AX is 0001h on success and 0000h on failure.
On an error, BL is 80h, 81h, 82h or 94h.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_LOCAL_DISABLE_A20 of its switch on AH.
SET_RESULT also stores 00h in BL on a success, a case the list does not give.
The XMS driver's AH=07h function queries the A20 line state.
AX is 0001h when the A20 line is enabled and 0000h when it is disabled.
BL is the error code 00h, 80h or 81h.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_QUERY_A20 of its switch on AH.
The XMS driver's AH=08h function queries the free extended memory.
The function takes BL as 00h, and some implementations leave BL unchanged on success.
AX is the size in KB of the largest free extended memory block.
DX is the total extended memory in KB.
BL is the error code 00h, 80h, 81h or A0h.
The returned sizes do not include the HMA.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_QUERY_FREE_EXTENDED_MEMORY of its switch on AH.
The case caps AX and DX at FFFFh.
The XMS driver's AH=09h function allocates an extended memory block.
DX is the number of kilobytes needed.
AX is 0001h on success and 0000h on failure.
On success, DX is the handle of the block.
On failure, BL is the error code 80h, 81h or A0h.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_ALLOCATE_EXTENDED_MEMORY of its switch on AH.
The helper stores A1h in BL when every handle is taken, a code the list does not give.
The XMS driver's AH=0Ah function frees an extended memory block.
DX is the handle of the block to free.
AX is 0001h on success and 0000h on failure.
On failure, BL is the error code 80h, 81h, A2h or ABh.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_FREE_EXTENDED_MEMORY of its switch on AH.
The XMS driver's AH=0Bh function moves an extended memory block.
DS:SI points to the move structure.
AX is 0001h on success and 0000h on failure.
On failure, BL is the error code 80h through 82h or A3h through A9h.
When either handle in the structure is 0000h, the corresponding offset is an absolute address in directly addressable memory.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_MOVE_EXTENDED_MEMORY_BLOCK of its switch on AH.
The XMS driver's AH=0Ch function locks an extended memory block.
DX is the handle of the block to lock.
AX is 0001h on success and 0000h on failure.
On success, DX:BX is the 32-bit physical address of the locked block.
On failure, BL is the error code 80h, 81h, A2h, ACh or ADh.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_LOCK_EXTENDED_MEMORY_BLOCK of its switch on AH.
BL keeps the caller's value on success: the case stores the helper's result in BL only when it is nonzero.
The XMS driver's AH=0Dh function unlocks an extended memory block.
DX is the handle of the block to unlock.
AX is 0001h on success and 0000h on failure.
On failure, BL is the error code 80h, 81h, A2h or AAh.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_UNLOCK_EXTENDED_MEMORY_BLOCK of its switch on AH.
The XMS driver's AH=0Eh function gets the information of an extended memory block.
DX is the handle to get information for.
AX is 0001h on success and 0000h on failure.
On success, BH is the block's lock count.
On success, BL is the number of free handles left.
On success, DX is the block size in KB.
On failure, BL is the error code 80h, 81h or A2h.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_GET_EMB_HANDLE_INFORMATION of its switch on AH.
The case truncates EDX to its low 16 bits before returning.
The XMS driver's AH=0Fh function resizes an extended memory block.
DX is the handle of the block.
BX is the new size of the block in KB.
AX is 0001h on success and 0000h on failure.
On failure, BL is the error code 80h, 81h, A0h through A2h or ABh.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_RESIZE_EXTENDED_MEMORY_BLOCK of its switch on AH.
The XMS driver's AH=10h function requests an upper memory block.
DX is the size of the block in paragraphs.
AX is 0001h on success and 0000h on failure.
On success, BX is the segment address of the UMB.
On success, DX is the actual size of the block; on failure, it is the largest available block.
On failure, BL is the error code 80h, B0h or B1h.
Upper memory is non-EMS memory between 640K and 1024K.
A driver need not implement functions 10h through 12h to be compliant with the standard.
Under DOS 5 and later, a CONFIG.SYS line DOS=UMB leaves no upper memory blocks to allocate.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_ALLOCATE_UMB of its switch on AH.
Before allocating, the case links the UMB chain into the MCB chain and searches UMBs only, then restores both.
The failure stores give DX 0 or the largest free block; on success the case never writes DX, so the caller reads back its request.
The XMS driver's AH=11h function releases an upper memory block.
DX is the segment address of the UMB to release.
AX is 0001h on success and 0000h on failure.
On failure, BL is the error code 80h or B2h.
A driver need not implement functions 10h through 12h to be compliant with the standard.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_DEALLOCATE_UMB of its switch on AH.
When the block cannot be freed, the case stores B1h in BL, a code the list does not give.
When UMBs are unavailable, the case stores 0000h in AX and 80h in BL.
The XMS v3.0 driver's AH=88h function queries the free extended memory.
EAX is the size in KB of the largest free extended memory block.
BL is the status 00h, 80h, 81h or A0h.
ECX is the physical address of the highest byte of memory, valid even on the error codes 81h and A0h.
EDX is the total extended memory in KB, and 0 when the status is A0h.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_QUERY_ANY_FREE_MEMORY of its switch on AH.
The XMS v3.0 driver's AH=89h function allocates any extended memory.
EDX is the number of kilobytes needed.
AX is 0001h on success and 0000h on failure.
On success, DX is the handle of the allocated block.
On failure, BL is the status 80h, 81h, A0h, A1h or A2h.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_ALLOCATE_ANY_MEMORY of its switch on AH.
The XMS v3.0 driver's AH=8Eh function gets the information of an extended memory block.
DX is the handle.
AX is 0001h on success and 0000h on failure.
On success, BH is the block's lock count.
On success, CX is the number of free handles left.
On success, EDX is the block size in KB.
On failure, BL is the status 80h, 81h or A2h.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_GET_EMB_HANDLE_INFORMATION_EXT of its switch on AH.
The XMS v3.0 driver's AH=8Fh function reallocates an extended memory block of any size.
DX is the handle of the unlocked block.
EBX is the new size in KB.
AX is 0001h on success and 0000h on failure.
On failure, BL is the status 80h, 81h, A0h through A2h or ABh.
The XMS driver reaches it by case XMS_RESIZE_ANY_EXTENDED_MEMORY_BLOCK of its switch on AH.
